haiku-low.q2: It gets 429 with a login page saying try again later. No password check, nothing recorded, and the lockout is not extended.
haiku-low.q3: It is destroyed. The old session row is deleted in the same transaction, and a brand-new session ID is issued.
haiku-low.q4: Only an opaque random session ID, in cookie sid. It is HttpOnly, so page scripts cannot read it. It is also Secure, SameSite=Lax, Path=/.
haiku-low.q5: The session ends 12 hours after login, even with constant activity. Separately, 30 minutes without requests also ends it.
haiku-low.q6: It deletes any row for that hash, clears the cookie, and redirects with 302 to /login.
haiku-low.q7: It deletes the session row for the cookie's hash and commits before replying. If no session exists, zero rows is fine; it clears the cookie and redirects to /login.
haiku-low.q8: In a sessions table in the shared Postgres database. Any instance looks up the cookie's hash there, so instances need no sticky sessions.
haiku-low.q9: In the login_failures table, keyed by lowercase email with a failed_at timestamp. Failures are counted when failed_at is within the last 10 minutes.
haiku-low.q10: It checks id_hash matches, last_seen_at is within 30 minutes, and expires_at is in the future, all using Postgres now(). If valid, it writes last_seen_at = now().

haiku-low.q12: A cleanup job on each instance, every 5 minutes, deletes sessions idle over 30 minutes or past expires_at.

sonnet.q1: It doesn't differ. Both get 401 with the same login page and the text "Invalid email or password". Unknown emails run bcrypt against a dummy hash so timing is the same too.
sonnet.q2: The attempt is refused with 429 (a login page saying to try again later). There is no user lookup or password check, nothing is recorded, and the lockout is not extended. Lockout lasts 15 minutes.
sonnet.q3: The server always issues a brand-new session ID, not derived from the old one. In the same transaction it deletes the row for the old cookie's hash, so the old session is destroyed.
sonnet.q4: Only the random session ID (32 random bytes, base64url). Page scripts cannot read it because the cookie is HttpOnly (it is also Secure and SameSite=Lax).
sonnet.q5: At the absolute limit, 12 hours after login (expires_at is fixed at login), whatever the activity. The idle limit never triggers because they keep using the app.
sonnet.q6: The UPDATE returns no row. The app deletes any session row for that hash, clears the cookie, and redirects (302) to /login.
sonnet.q7: The server runs DELETE FROM sessions for the sid hash and commits before replying. If there is no cookie or the session is already gone, zero rows deleted is not an error. It still clears the cookie and replies 302 /login.
sonnet.q8: In the sessions table in the shared Postgres (no Redis, no sticky sessions). Any instance hashes the cookie's ID with SHA-256 and looks up id_hash (the primary key) in Postgres.
sonnet.q9: In the login_failures table (email, failed_at) in Postgres, keyed by the submitted lowercase email string, with lockouts in login_lockouts. The window is the count of that email's failures in the last 10 minutes, using Postgres now() for the comparison.
sonnet.q10: It compares the hash of the session ID (id_hash), last_seen_at (must be within the last 30 minutes), and expires_at (must be in the future) against Postgres now(), in one UPDATE statement. When valid, it writes last_seen_at = now() and returns user_id.
sonnet.q11: The transaction rolls back, no session is issued, and the browser gets the 503 "Something went wrong on our side. Please try again in a moment." page, with no cookie set.
sonnet.q12: The cleanup job. It runs every 5 minutes on each instance and deletes sessions idle over 30 minutes or past expires_at. It only saves space, because expired rows are already invalid.
